data.why: The repo's bundled example data is only the 8 species reference cross-section spectra (not measurable sample spectra), so two-column wavelength/intensity files matching the documented SpectraSuite-like upload format were synthesized: a lamp reference spectrum plus measured spectra with an O3 Hartley-band and NO gamma-band absorption dip built in (210-400 nm, matching the bundled cross sections and WAVE_LOW/WAVE_HIGH defaults), including an intensity spike (saturation/cosmic-ray outlier at 340 nm) and a missing reading (NaN at 365 nm) in measured.txt to exercise the app's robustness, plus a 3-frame time series (Source_70_2_0000{0,1,2}.txt) with increasing absorption depth to exercise the time-series/trend path.

goals: Upload a reference (I0) and measured (It) spectrum and deconvolve it into number densities for the 8 species (HONO, HONO2, N2O4, N2O5, NO, NO2, NO3, O3) via NNLS linear regression
Inspect the fit quality (R2, RMSE, MAE, MAPE) and the measured-vs-reconstructed optical-depth overlay to judge whether the deconvolution is trustworthy
Tune the advanced fit heuristics (OD clipping threshold, false-positive suppression coefficient, NO band alignment/FWHM, O3 tail refinement) to resolve a tricky or noisy spectrum
Upload a time-series of spectra sharing one I0 and track how a species' number density evolves over the series (time-series trend plot)
Download the per-species results (chemical table / CSV) for a run to keep as a local record of the analysis
Compare the NNLS linear-regression path against the ResNet machine-learning path as a quick first-pass check on a novel spectrum

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-evidenced tree of the app's real job: turning reference and measured UV spectra into number densities for 8 species, judging the fit, and exporting, in both single and time-series modes. Every sampled screen matches its node. Before filing, it needs small fixes: split the oversized heuristics feature, add the series uploader as a feature, say that the README's machine-learning path no longer exists in the code, and give the community-contribution side at least a blocked task.
